forecasts.question: Will at least 50 commercial vessels per day transit the Strait of Hormuz (50%+ of pre-war ~120/day baseline) during any consecutive 7-day window before EOD 2026-06-10?
forecasts.delta_reason: No material movement. Zero commercial vessels transited Hormuz on May 18 and May 19 (two consecutive days) per Windward/Hormuz Strait Monitor data. Lloyd’s war-risk premium remains approximately 5% of hull value — more than 20 times pre-war levels. All major carriers (Maersk, CMA CGM, MSC, Hapag-Lloyd) have confirmed suspension of scheduled Hormuz transits. Iran’s PGSA toll regime, operational since May 5, charges up to $2 million per vessel in Chinese yuan or Bitcoin per Lloyd’s List; US- and Israel-linked vessels are categorically excluded. The Israeli strike-preparation intelligence report (CNN May 20) creates additional uncertainty over any near-term diplomatic resolution that would enable safe commercial transit. No indicator observed.
forecasts.resolution_criteria: YES if Hormuz Strait Monitor (or UNCTAD, or Lloyd’s List) reports ≥50 daily transits averaged over 7 consecutive days within the horizon window. NO if average stays below 50/day for the full horizon window.
forecasts.resolution_source_rule: Hormuz Strait Monitor (primary), Lloyd’s List Intelligence (secondary), UNCTAD Maritime Trade quarterly report (lagging confirmation).
forecasts.ambiguity_rule: If only Iranian-flagged or sanctions-evading dark-fleet vessels make up the count, but Western insurers still refuse: AMBIGUOUS-RESOLVE-AS-NO (the operationally meaningful question is whether Western shipping has returned). PGSA addendum (Judge, 2026-05-19): third-country vessels (Chinese, Indian, Turkish) transiting under Iran’s Persian Gulf Strait Authority toll regime count ONLY IF ≥2 of Hormuz Strait Monitor/Lloyd’s List/UNCTAD/Windward confirm them as independent commercial entities not under IRGC-linked tolls; PGSA self-reported numbers are excluded from resolution sourcing.

indicators.name: Lloyd's war-risk premium reduced below 1.5% of hull
indicators.expected_effect: +20pp toward YES; insurance is the binding constraint on commercial transit.

indicators.name: Maersk/MSC/Frontline announce return to scheduled Hormuz transit
indicators.expected_effect: +25pp toward YES; major shipping lines lead the resumption.

forecasts.question: Will Netanyahu's governing coalition lose its 61-seat Knesset majority (via defection, dissolution motion, or no-confidence) before the mandatory 2026-10-27 election date?
forecasts.delta_reason: No material movement — weekly cadence only (reviewed Sundays). NOTE for Sunday May 24 review: Coalition submitted Knesset dissolution bill May 13 (co-sponsored by Degel HaTorah, Shas, Religious Zionist, Otzma Yehudit per JNS), and preliminary vote held May 20. This is a major development bearing directly on resolution criteria. Full re-reasoning and cold-start audit at Sunday May 24.
forecasts.resolution_criteria: YES if a Knesset roll-call vote confirms coalition loss of majority (61 seats), OR if Netanyahu announces early dissolution and election date moves earlier than 2026-10-27. NO if coalition survives to mandatory election date with 61+ seats intact.
forecasts.resolution_source_rule: Knesset official record + Reuters/Haaretz/Times of Israel confirmation. Polling alone does not resolve.
forecasts.ambiguity_rule: If coalition drops below 61 but Netanyahu remains caretaker PM until election: counts as YES (majority lost). If a single party (e.g. Smotrich) departs but coalition retains 61+: counts as NO. Reviewed weekly only (Sundays); no intra-week deltas allowed per Codex DA #12.

indicators.expected_effect: +20pp toward YES if observed; would also trigger Haredi reconsideration.

forecasts.question: Will Iran and the US confirm a signed written framework agreement (any named successor to the 14-point MOU) before EOD 2026-06-05?
forecasts.delta_reason: Updated 0.25 → 0.20. Three independent negative factors from May 18-20: (1) CNN reported May 20 that new US intelligence shows Israel preparing a possible strike on Iranian nuclear facilities, citing multiple US officials (Times of Israel, JPost); (2) Araghchi in Istanbul for EU talks May 20 warned that reinstating UN snapback sanctions would have ‘irreversible’ consequences (Time), a hardening posture not consistent with imminent signing; (3) Iran’s counter-proposal via Pakistan (~May 18, JPost/Al Jazeera) rejected the 20-year enrichment moratorium and proposed dilution rather than transfer of the 440kg 60%-enriched stockpile — a gap the US has not accepted. No Witkoff-Araghchi direct meeting confirmed.
forecasts.resolution_criteria: YES if a named US administration official AND a named Iranian official publicly confirm a signed written framework (by any name); OR if the document text is published by Axios/Reuters/State Dept or Iran MFA with both parties acknowledging authenticity. Verbal ‘agreement in principle’ does not count.
forecasts.resolution_source_rule: At minimum, Reuters AND one of Axios/AP/AFP quoting named US AND Iranian principals (not envoys alone). Official Iranian Foreign Ministry statement or State Dept press release also resolves.
forecasts.ambiguity_rule: Agreement by envoys only, without principal confirmation (Trump/Pezeshkian) within 72h of announcement = AMBIGUOUS-RESOLVE-AS-NO. If Iran signs but Khamenei’s office disavows within 72h = AMBIGUOUS-RESOLVE-AS-NO.

indicators.name: Witkoff/Araghchi direct meeting confirmed (not via Pakistan)
indicators.expected_effect: +15pp toward YES; direct principal-level engagement removed the Pakistani-channel lag in April.

indicators.name: Trump public statement calling deal 'beautiful' or 'done'
indicators.expected_effect: +20pp toward YES; Trump’s typical pre-announcement framing on social media has been a leading indicator.

forecasts.question: Will the Lebanon 45-day ceasefire extension (announced May 15) formally collapse — defined as US withdrawal of sponsorship OR Lebanese government publicly declaring the truce void — before EOD 2026-05-22?
forecasts.delta_reason: No material movement. IDF strikes on May 15-20 confirmed in Tyre and Nabatieh districts (south Lebanon), not Beirut governorate — consistent with ambiguity_rule exclusion. IDF Chief Zamir’s “no ceasefire” declaration is an operational statement, not a formal US or Lebanese government withdrawal. State Dept reaffirmed the extension on May 15 (PBS/CNBC); June 2-3 political talks and May 29 Pentagon security track remain on schedule. No indicator observed.
forecasts.resolution_criteria: YES if the US State Department or Lebanese Foreign Ministry issues a public statement explicitly declaring the ceasefire void or withdrawn; OR if IDF and Hezbollah resume sustained exchange at pre-April-16 intensity (>50 launches/day from each side) and both US and Lebanon acknowledge breakdown. Individual violations — which are continuous — do NOT resolve YES.
forecasts.resolution_source_rule: US State Dept press release or named spokesperson; OR Lebanese government official quoted in Reuters/AP/AFP; OR combined IDF/LBAF situation reports showing pre-truce intensity levels.
forecasts.ambiguity_rule: IDF strikes in south Lebanon outside Beirut governorate = NOT collapse (consistent with current porous-truce pattern). Hezbollah verbal threat to resume without acting = NOT collapse. Collapse requires formal withdrawal of US or Lebanese government support.

indicators.name: IDF airstrike on Beirut governorate within 72h of ceasefire extension
indicators.expected_effect: +20pp toward YES; would demonstrate US tolerance for truce violation at capital level.

indicators.name: Hezbollah rocket barrage >50/day from south Litani
indicators.expected_effect: +15pp toward YES; mass rocket fire historically triggers Israeli large-scale response and truce void.

forecasts.question: Will Netanyahu formally announce an early election date earlier than the mandatory 2026-10-27 date before EOD 2026-06-01?
forecasts.delta_reason: Updated 0.22 → 0.12. Coalition submitted dissolution bill May 13 (JNS, Times of Israel, Washington Post) and preliminary Knesset reading scheduled May 20. However: (a) the bill does not name an election date — date to be set by Knesset House Committee at least 90 days after final passage; (b) the bill is at preliminary reading only, requiring committee deliberations and three further Knesset readings before becoming law. Netanyahu has not made a formal Knesset speech naming a pre-October-27 election date. The probability that a formal announcement meeting resolution criteria occurs before EOD June 1 — while the bill is still at preliminary stage — is structurally low.
forecasts.resolution_criteria: YES if Netanyahu makes a formal Knesset speech or public announcement naming an election date earlier than 2026-10-27; OR if the Knesset passes a formal dissolution motion by majority vote. Leaks and media speculation do NOT resolve.
forecasts.resolution_source_rule: Times of Israel, Haaretz, or Channel 12/13 news citing direct Netanyahu statement or official Knesset vote record. Reuters/AP confirmation required for international sources.
forecasts.ambiguity_rule: Coalition partner threatening dissolution without a formal Knesset vote = NOT resolved. Netanyahu ‘considering’ elections per aides = NOT resolved. Only a formal announcement by Netanyahu himself or a passed dissolution vote counts.

indicators.name: Degel HaTorah co-sponsors Knesset dissolution bill
indicators.expected_effect: Observed May 13 (JNS/ToI). Coalition dissolution process underway — necessary but not sufficient for F2 resolution before June 1.

indicators.expected_effect: +10pp toward YES; strong opposition polling removes Netanyahu’s rationale for delay.

forecasts.question: Will the Israeli Knesset dissolution bill pass its third and final reading — formally dissolving the Knesset and triggering early elections — before EOD 2026-06-10?
forecasts.delta_reason: Initial assignment. Dissolution bill submitted May 13 with cross-coalition co-sponsorship (Degel HaTorah, Shas, Religious Zionist, Otzma Yehudit per JNS). Preliminary reading scheduled May 20. Bill still requires committee deliberations and three readings. Haredi factions (who want September elections) and the coalition both have incentive to move quickly. Competing opposition bill also submitted. Legislative calendar of 21 days is tight but not impossible for a dissolution bill where all main coalition parties are aligned. p=0.55 reflects genuine coalition co-sponsorship but recognises natural parliamentary process delays.
forecasts.resolution_criteria: YES if the Knesset conducts an official roll-call vote on the third reading of the dissolution bill and a majority of MKs vote in favour; OR if the Knesset’s official website (knesset.gov.il) confirms the bill has passed third reading and dissolution is in effect. A preliminary reading alone does NOT count. Committee approval does NOT count. Only final third-reading passage counts.
forecasts.resolution_source_rule: Knesset official website (knesset.gov.il) vote record, confirmed by Reuters AND at least one of: Times of Israel, Haaretz, or Channel 12/13 news. Israeli government press office confirmation also acceptable.
forecasts.ambiguity_rule: If the bill passes third reading but is immediately challenged at the Supreme Court and a stay is granted within 72h: AMBIGUOUS-RESOLVE-AS-NO until stay is lifted. If the vote is split and Speaker declares a tie or parliamentary procedure dispute: AMBIGUOUS until ruled. If coalition pulls the bill between readings: RESOLVE-NO.

indicators.name: Knesset second reading committee approval of dissolution bill
indicators.expected_effect: +20pp toward YES; committee passage is a necessary precursor to third reading.

indicators.name: Haaretz or ToI reports third-reading vote date set by Knesset House Committee
indicators.expected_effect: +15pp toward YES; scheduling confirms parliamentary majority has committed.

forecasts.question: Will Israel carry out a confirmed kinetic strike on at least one Iranian nuclear facility (defined as sites on the IAEA's declared Iranian nuclear programme list — Natanz, Fordow, Isfahan, Arak) before EOD 2026-06-20?
forecasts.delta_reason: Initial assignment. CNN reported May 20 that new US intelligence, based on intercepted Israeli communications and observed military movements, concludes Israel has been making preparations for a possible strike on Iranian nuclear facilities (confirmed independently by Times of Israel and Jerusalem Post). No final decision has been confirmed. Trump administration stated it is unlikely to help Israel carry out such strikes. DA caution noted: this CNN intelligence-preparation pattern matches prior chronic reports (March 2026) that did not lead to action within 30 days. p=0.20 reflects the genuine but non-determinative nature of the preparation intelligence, US opposition, and the open diplomatic track.
forecasts.resolution_criteria: YES if the IDF, Israeli government, or US DoD publicly confirms an Israeli strike on any IAEA-declared Iranian nuclear facility; OR if IAEA Director-General issues a public statement confirming physical damage at a declared Iranian nuclear site; OR if satellite imagery analyzed by ≥2 independent OSINT providers (Planet Labs/Maxar/UNOSAT) confirms crater or structural damage at a declared nuclear site. Iranian denial alone does NOT resolve NO — requires independent physical verification or IDF/US DoD statement.
forecasts.resolution_source_rule: Reuters AND AP/AFP quoting named IDF spokesperson or DoD official; OR IAEA Director-General public statement; OR Israeli PM/Defense Minister public address naming the target site. OSINT satellite confirmation requires ≥2 independent providers.
forecasts.ambiguity_rule: IDF strikes on Iranian military targets outside declared nuclear sites (e.g. IRGC bases, missile depots) = NOT resolved. Cyber attack on nuclear facilities without physical damage = NOT resolved. Strike preparation or sorties that do not reach targets = NOT resolved. If Iran claims strike occurred but IDF denies and no physical satellite evidence available: AMBIGUOUS-RESOLVE-AS-NO at horizon.

indicators.name: US-Israel diplomatic consultations reported to break down over strike timing (NYT/Washington Post/Haaretz)
indicators.expected_effect: +15pp toward YES; diplomatic rupture historically precedes unilateral Israeli action.

indicators.name: IAEA announces emergency Board of Governors meeting citing credible threat to Iranian facilities
indicators.expected_effect: +20pp toward YES; IAEA emergency meetings have preceded or immediately followed kinetic events.
